text: bixverse R package wraps bioinformatics computational biology methods (gene set enrichment, graphs, co-expression modules, ontologies, full single cell suite) around Rust core exposed via rextendr/extendr. official Windows support (h5 toolchain cross-compilation blocker).

title: CLAUDE.md
text: heavy numerical code live repo. sits standalone bixverse-rs crate, declared src/rust/Cargo.toml features single-cell + multi-modal. usually redirected [patch.crates-io] block, see “Local development” . Everything src/rust/src/ thin extendr binding layer, one module per domain (base, data, enrichment, graph, meta_cell, methods, ontology, single_cell), registered src/rust/src/lib.rs via extendr_module!. Algorithmic work belongs bixverse-rs; repo gets binding plus R wrapper. R/extendr-wrappers.R generated compilation (cargo run --bin document, see src/rust/document.rs). Never edit hand. Exposed Rust functions prefixed rs_*; R wrapper input validation.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Files grouped prefix: classes_*.R - class definitions (S7 mostly, R6 encapsulation needed) methods_*.R - S7 generics methods classes functions_*.R - plain procedural functions param_wrappers.R / param_constructors.R - params_*() functions returning validated parameter lists checkmate_extensions.R - checkX() / assertX() pairs built checkmate::makeAssertionFunction(), mostly validating parameter lists Every exported function validates inputs checkmate. Parameter bundles passed lists built params_*() validated matching assert*Params(). BixverseBaseClass (R/base_class.R) S7 root providing get_params() / get_results(); analysis classes inherit . R/classes_union.R defines S7 unions (e.g. ScOrMc = SingleCells | MetaCells) methods can shared. Small result objects use plain S3; print methods must registered manually R/zzz.R (S7/S3 interaction quirk).

title: CLAUDE.md
text: SingleCells (R/classes_single_cell_.R) holds counts memory. handle directory containing: counts_cells.bin / counts_genes.bin - Rust binary count format, accessed SingleCellCountData extendr object (env-based class, R6) sc_duckdb.db - obs/var tables via SingleCellDuckDB R6 class (R/classes_single_cell_db.R) Two lightweight S3 side-cars ride along S7 object: ScMap (gene/cell name index maps, cells--keep, HVG indices) ScCache (PCA factors, embeddings, kNN, sNN graph). SingleCellsMultiModal extends additional assay layers (currently ADT). Gotcha: ScMap stores 0-based indices Rust. Setters like set_cells_to_keep() subtract 1 way ; anything reading slots handing back R must add 1.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: info/code_style.md authoritative document. essentials: KISS. Avoid deep inheritance speculative abstraction. Document everything roxygen2; assert every input checkmate. data.table tibble/data.frame. purrr::map* apply family. Anything beyond simple reshaping/aggregation goes Rust. Avoid new R dependencies; Rust dependencies fine. 80 column limit, enforced air. emojis anywhere. Vignettes quarto (.qmd vignettes/), site config _pkgdown.yml. Version bumps DESCRIPTION main auto-tag cut GitHub release; keep src/rust/Cargo.toml version sync.

title: Gene set analysis and GRN inference on PBMCs

title: Gene set analysis and GRN inference on PBMCs
text: SCENIC infers gene regulatory networks asking: gene, transcription factors (TFs) best predict expression? original implementation uses either random forests GRNBoost2 (gradient boosted trees) regress target gene TFs, extracts feature importances proxy regulatory strength. bixverse implementation re-implements Rust several optimisations make RF ExtraTrees paths substantially faster single-target---time approach used GRNBoost2: Quantisation: TF expression values discretised 256 bins (u8), histogram construction tree building operates single bytes fits comfortably L1 cache. Multi-output batching: 64 target genes share single tree structure. histogram construction cost paid per node per feature, split score aggregates variance reduction across targets batch. amortises dominant cost tree building across targets. Correlated gene batching: rather assigning genes batches randomly, optional SVD + k-means step groups co-expressed genes together shared tree structure informative target batch. GRNBoost2 histogram subtraction: gradient boosted path (single-target), code builds full-feature histograms node derives larger child via parent-minus-smaller subtraction, avoiding redundant scan larger child’s samples. OOB early stopping prevents overfitting main source speedup. 2,700-cell PBMC3k dataset optimisations noticeable… data small method take long. datasets tens thousands cells thousands TFs, RF/ET multi-output path comfortably outperforms GRNBoost2. need just decide okay batching genes. Generally speaking, big signals recovered (empirical testing). SCENIC first filters genes minimum total counts minimum proportion expressing cells remove uninformative targets. need list known TFs. Aerts lab provides curated list human can download map Ensembl IDs. genes TFs hand, run GRN inference step. use random forests batch size 64 illustrate multi-output path. bored, can run methods (learner_type = "grnboost2") compare importance scores. see high correlations (can explore speed differences…) raw importance matrix large noisy. next steps winnow candidate regulatory network keeping top TF-gene pairs filtering pairwise expression correlation. approach used per gene TFs importance score ≥ mean(importance_score) + n_sd * sd(importance_score) per given gene kept. Note n_sd adjusted depending learner: RF ExtraTrees spread importance evenly across TFs GRNBoost2, lower threshold (e.g. n_sd = 1) appropriate, whereas GRNBoost2 concentrates importance onto fewer TFs tolerates n_sd = 1.5 even n_sd = 2. final (optional) step SCENIC pipeline validates predicted TF-gene links known motif binding sites. requires downloading CisTarget motif ranking database motif--TF annotation files Aerts lab resources, together roughly 400 MB. therefore show code evaluate default. CisTarget pass/fail filter module. Per enriched motif builds recovery curve, compares mean + 2 SD curve across every motif database, keeps genes point maximum separation. expect regulons coming build_regulons() good deal smaller modules going . run regulon binarisation. work types "bag genes" analyses single cell bixverse.

text: raw importance matrix large noisy. next steps winnow candidate regulatory network keeping top TF-gene pairs filtering pairwise expression correlation. approach used per gene TFs importance score ≥ mean(importance_score) + n_sd * sd(importance_score) per given gene kept. Note n_sd adjusted depending learner: RF ExtraTrees spread importance evenly across TFs GRNBoost2, lower threshold (e.g. n_sd = 1) appropriate, whereas GRNBoost2 concentrates importance onto fewer TFs tolerates n_sd = 1.5 even n_sd = 2.

text: final (optional) step SCENIC pipeline validates predicted TF-gene links known motif binding sites. requires downloading CisTarget motif ranking database motif--TF annotation files Aerts lab resources, together roughly 400 MB. therefore show code evaluate default. CisTarget pass/fail filter module. Per enriched motif builds recovery curve, compares mean + 2 SD curve across every motif database, keeps genes point maximum separation. expect regulons coming build_regulons() good deal smaller modules going . run regulon binarisation. work types "bag genes" analyses single cell bixverse.
code: # Download the CisTarget reference files (cached after first download) paths <- download_cistarget_hg38()  rankings <- read_motif_ranking(paths$rankings) annotations <- read_motif_annotation_file(paths$motif_annotations)  # Run motif enrichment on the TF-gene links scenic_res <- tf_to_genes_motif_enrichment(   x = scenic_res,   motif_rankings = rankings,   annot_data = annotations,   # we store everything as Ensembl... The SCENIC data has gene symbols, hence,   # the need to provide conversion   gene_id_to_symbol = ensembl_to_symbol,   cis_target_params = params_cistarget(),   only_high_conf_tf = FALSE,   .verbose = TRUE )  # CisTarget results per TF cistarget_dt <- get_cistarget_res(scenic_res) head(cistarget_dt[order(-nes)])  # The TF-to-gene table now has a leading_edge column indicating which # genes fall within the motif recovery curve tf_gene_final <- get_tf_to_gene(scenic_res)  head(tf_gene_final[(in_leading_edge)][order(-importance)]) # build_regulons() applies that filter, adds the TF back to its own set and # drops anything too small. This is what you hand to aucell_sc() regulons <- build_regulons(scenic_res)  auc_regulons <- aucell_sc(   object = sc_object,   gs_list = regulons,   aucell_params = params_sc_aucell() )  binarised_regulons <- binarise_regulon_activity(auc_regulons)  binary_matrix <- binarised_regulons$binary colnames(binary_matrix) <- ensembl_to_symbol[colnames(binary_matrix)]  sc_object[["STAT1_active"]] <- binary_matrix[, "STAT1"]  embedding_plot_sc(   object = sc_object,   embedding = "umap",   colour_by = "STAT1_active" )

Bulk co-expression modules
text: Bulk co-expression module detection tries find groups genes vary together across samples. bixverse ships five approaches shared BulkCoExp class: CoReMo (Srivastava, et al.: hierarchical clustering RBF-transformed correlation matrix. Fast, deterministic, gives signed modules per-sample eigengenes. Graph-based Leiden (Barrio-Hernandez, et al.) — build sparse affinity graph correlations, cluster Leiden. Great want tunable resolution hierarchical sub-clustering. ICA — independent component analysis stability across random initialisations. component picks independent signal; genes tails component’s loading distribution define module. DGRDL (Pan, et al.) — dual graph-regularised dictionary learning. Sparse decomposition regularised feature- sample-side Laplacians. NMF (HALS) — non-negative matrix factorisation hierarchical alternating least squares. Non-negative loadings give natural “parts-based” module interpretation per-sample module activity. One structural difference matters throughout. CoReMo Leiden partition genes: one gene, one module. three factorisation methods , . gene can load several components, get_modules() returns one row per (gene, component) pair ICA, NMF DGRDL, genes component’s tail appear nowhere. params_module_membership() controls thresholding. assume gene unique key. title: Doublet detection with bixverse
text: Doublets - droplets containing two cells - common artefact droplet-based single cell experiments. left undetected, masquerade intermediate cell states novel populations quietly corrupt downstream analyses. vignette demonstrates three doublet detection approaches available bixverse benchmarks ground truth calls demuxlet, identifies doublets via genetic variation across pooled donors. bixverse provides three computational doublet detection methods: Scrublet simulation-based approach (Wolock, et al., 2019). generates synthetic doublets averaging pairs randomly selected cells, embeds real synthetic cells together, scores real cell proportion nearest neighbours synthetic. bimodal score distribution expected: singlets cluster near zero, doublets near one. threshold score determines final calls. Boosted doublet detection takes different angle. pos_actual = "DBL" ) {   tp <- sum(predicted == pos_predicted & actual == pos_actual)   fp <- sum(predicted == pos_predicted & actual != pos_actual)   fn <- sum(predicted != pos_predicted & actual == what: Gene Ontology-aware enrichment: the elimination method
title: Gene Set Enrichment Methods
text: naive approach running hypergeometric test independently GO term produces heavily redundant results, significant child terms mechanically inflate ancestors. elimination method Adrian et al. addresses traversing ontology specific terms (leaves) upwards. term reaches significance threshold, genes annotated term removed ancestor terms tests computed. means ancestor terms tested residual signal already explained specific descendants, yielding results less redundant interpretable. bixverse ships human GO data exposes via dedicated S7 class transfers ontology structure Rust efficient traversal. interface mirrors generic hypergeometric functions: single target set list, Rust’s ownership model ensuring ontology structure shared across tests without copying, keeping memory overhead low. version lists: DAG traversal inherently sequential per gene set (level depends one ), tests within level parallelised via rayon. what: Alternative: post-hoc simplification of GO results
title: Gene Set Enrichment Methods
text: alternative strategy run unconstrained hypergeometric test GO terms collapse redundant results afterwards using semantic similarity. approach flexible — can apply enrichment results, just produced bixverse — adjust test statistics way elimination method . Whether prefer pre-hoc elimination post-hoc simplification depends use case; exploratory analyses simplification approach can convenient, rigorous GO reporting elimination method generally preferable. simplification uses Wang semantic similarity group related terms, retains term best test statistic within cluster. Ties FDR broken ontology depth, preferring specific term.

text: Meta cells small groups transcriptionally similar cells aggregated single representative profile. motivation twofold: firstly, single cell counts sparse noisy, many downstream methods (correlation networks, GRN inference, archetype-based modelling) behave poorly raw single cell data. Aggregating meta cells reduces sparsity preserving heterogeneity bulk pseudo-replicates average . Secondly, reduce computational burden substantially. bixverse provides three meta cell algorithms different underlying ideas: hdWGCNA-style meta cells (Morabito, et al., 2023) iterate kNN graph, picking seed cells aggregating neighbours, constraint many cells two meta cells allowed share. Simple, fast reasonably effective. Works directly kNN graph. SEACells (Persad, et al., 2023) uses kernel archetypal analysis. algorithm finds set archetypes (SEACells) every cell can expressed convex combination nearby archetypes. Tends produce purer aggregations computationally expensive three. SuperCells (Bilous, et al., 2022) applies walktrap community detection algorithm kNN graph treats community meta cell. Granularity controlled indirectly graining factor (average number cells per meta cell). Protein panels tiny: dozens antibodies, sometimes couple hundred larger commercial panels. cost-benefit calculus justifies -disk binary format RNA just hold . Even million cells times 200 proteins fits memory without breaking sweat. whole ADTCounts object — raw counts, normalised counts, bit metadata — lives memory plain matrix. saving code complexity rather RAM. normalisation, currently two options: CLR (centred log-ratio): Seurat default. Comes two flavours via seurat_clr: original CLR (allows negatives) modified Seurat-style version (). DSB (denoised scaled background): Mulè et al., 2022. principled empty droplets estimate protein background; falls back 2-component k-means log counts (“ModelNegativeADTnorm” path). Isotype controls help DSB tease apart per-cell technical noise true biological signal. detect_adt_isotypes() regexes obvious patterns (IgG.*, Ig.*ctrl, etc.) fine standard TotalSeq panels; anything unusual just pass column names directly via isotype_names.

title: Multi-modal single cell analysis with bixverse
text: ADT design philosophy differs RNA. Protein panels tiny: dozens antibodies, sometimes couple hundred larger commercial panels. cost-benefit calculus justifies -disk binary format RNA just hold . Even million cells times 200 proteins fits memory without breaking sweat. whole ADTCounts object — raw counts, normalised counts, bit metadata — lives memory plain matrix. saving code complexity rather RAM. normalisation, currently two options: CLR (centred log-ratio): Seurat default. Comes two flavours via seurat_clr: original CLR (allows negatives) modified Seurat-style version (). DSB (denoised scaled background): Mulè et al., 2022. principled empty droplets estimate protein background; falls back 2-component k-means log counts (“ModelNegativeADTnorm” path). Isotype controls help DSB tease apart per-cell technical noise true biological signal. detect_adt_isotypes() regexes obvious patterns (IgG.*, Ig.*ctrl, etc.) fine standard TotalSeq panels; anything unusual just pass column names directly via isotype_names.

title: Multi-modal single cell analysis with bixverse
text: far looked modality isolation. single cell-type assignment uses , want joint representation. current implementation bixverse Weighted Nearest Neighbours (WNN) Hao et al., 2021, method Seurat v4 introduced. intuition different modalities carry different information different cells. something like monocyte versus B cell, RNA signal strong. CD4 versus CD8 T cell subsets, protein signal much cleaner — mRNAs barely differential resolution. WNN formalises : cell, asks well cell’s neighbours one modality predict profile modality, uses answer weight two modalities per cell. weighted neighbours merged single joint graph. whole thing runs Rust — per-cell weights, neighbour selection, graph merging — scales hundreds thousands cells comfortably. resulting graph lands other_data$wnn can embedded just like modality. nice sanity check look marker modalities, projected onto WNN embedding. WNN job, two pictures largely agree — even though come completely independent measurements.  , rest pipeline (clustering, marker detection, cell type annotation) works exactly standard vignette — just point relevant functions WNN graph instead RNA one.
code: sc_object <- generate_wnn_graph_sc(   sc_object,   wnn_params = params_sc_wnn(sd_scale = 1) ) #> Running WNN graph generation. #> Generating sNN graph (full: TRUE) from WNN graph. #> Transforming sNN data to igraph. sc_object <- tsne_sc(   sc_object,   modality = "wnn" ) #> Running t-SNE. #> Using provided kNN graph. p1 <- feature_plot_sc(   sc_object,   features = "ENSG00000167286",   feature_labels = c(ENSG00000167286 = "CD3D_rna"),   embedding = "tsne",   expr_modality = "rna",   embd_modality = "wnn",   point_size = 1 )  p2 <- feature_plot_sc(   sc_object,   features = "CD3D",   feature_labels = c(CD3D = "CD3D_adt"),   embedding = "tsne",   expr_modality = "adt",   embd_modality = "wnn",   point_size = 1 )  p1 + p2

title: NicheNet ligand-receptor analysis with bixverse

NicheNet ranks upstream ligands well predicted target gene sets align gene set interest receiver cell type. pipeline : Build ligand-target regulatory potential matrix signalling network (PPI) gene regulatory network (GRN). Define gene set interest receiver (, T-cell marker genes). Score ligand well targets overlap gene set (AUROC, AUPR, correlations). Combine ligand activity sender/receiver expression DE single prioritisation score.

title: Analysing PBMCs with bixverse
text: Leiden clustering followed differential gene expression across clusters. can also run Louvain want, Leiden thought better properties, see Traag, et al.. case large data sets option run accelerated form clustering. runs first k-means clustering (default sqrt(N) cells), kNN centroids, followed Louvain (Leiden yet supported, -list) across set resolutions. also option run across several seeds check stability clustering. ran grid search, membership want explore k-means memberships centroids, getters . can add data object via: Let us run quickly UMAP tSNE. can use bixverse.plots package provides basic plotting functions : Plotting embedding using embedding_plot_sc check UMAP embeddings:  Let’s check tSNE  can also plot gene expression embedding space using feature_plot_sc:  Define set marker genes perform cell type annotation. Let’s annotate PBMCs using scType cell type annotation algorithm Ianevski et al. (2022). first prepare cell type markers right format using prepare_cell_markers helper functions. Subsequently calculate scType score using calc_sc_type_scores summarise cluster level get annotated cell type using score_clusters. Finally, can assign back cell type annotation sc_object. can add cell type annotation back sc_object.  Alternatively, can also show expression levels cell type markers using dotplot plotting function dot_plot_sc bixverse.plots.  addition feature plot (feature_plot_sc), can also represent gene expression using violin plot

title: Batch correction with bixverse
text: Batch effects systematic technical differences experimental runs can obscure genuine biological signal single cell data. datasets multiple experiments, technologies, laboratories combined, cells tend group source rather cell type. Batch correction methods aim remove technical artefacts whilst preserving biological variation. bixverse provides four batch correction approaches, different trade-offs: fastMNN (Haghverdi, et al., 2018) identifies mutual nearest neighbours across batches – pairs cells different batches ’s closest match. Correction vectors computed pairs applied align embeddings. particularly effective cell type composition differs across batches. Harmony (Korsunsky, et al., 2019) operates PCA embeddings using iterative soft clustering diversity penalties. assigns cells clusters, estimates batch effects per cluster via ridge regression, corrects embedding. tends fast works well across range scenarios. Additionally, version 2 released, see Patikas, et al., 2026 improvements increase scalability larger data sets modifications objective functions overcorrect across batches different cell types . BBKNN (Polanski, et al., 2020) takes fundamentally different approach. Rather correcting embedding, constructs batch-balanced k-nearest neighbour graph building separate neighbour indices per batch. corrected graph can used directly clustering visualisation. Seurat anchors (Stuart, et al., 2019) find pairs cells mutual nearest neighbours space shared two batches, score much neighbourhood share, use pull one batch onto . Two flavours available. CCA builds shared space canonical correlations corrects hardest, suits batches don’t share cell types. rPCA projects batch ’s PCA basis instead: cheaper, gentler, better default batches broadly match. need batch-aware HVGs. bixverse also provides three metrics assessing batch correction quality: kBET: tests whether neighbourhood batch proportions match global proportions (best embedding-based methods). Batch ASW: measures batch separation embedding space (best embedding-based methods). LISI: measures effective number batches per neighbourhood (works kNN graph).

text: write one sample CellRanger flat-file form point explicit params_sc_mtx_io() trio (real CellRanger output, convenience helper get_cell_ranger_params() auto-locates matrix.mtx / barcodes.tsv / genes.tsv). Two params_sc_mtx_io() arguments handle common deviations strict CellRanger convention: cells_as_rows – whether .mtx cells rows. CellRanger default FALSE (genes rows). title: Single-cell data I/O in bixverse
text: write_tenx_h5_sc() expects counts plus barcode vector features table (least id name). load_tenx_h5() reads gene-expression modality (V3 files may also carry e.g. Antibody Capture, filtered via feature_type). prescan_tenx_h5_files() takes named vector .h5 paths (names become sample identifiers), inspects file CellRanger version (v2 vs v3), filters requested feature_type, builds global gene space. load_multi_tenx_h5() mirrors multi-MTX / multi-h5ad workflow. gene_universe controls feature space reconciled across files: "intersection" keeps genes present every input. "union" keeps genes present input; cells file lacks given gene get zero counts . Mixed v2 / v3 inputs call handled transparently, non-gene modalities (e.g. Antibody Capture) silently dropped feature_type = "Gene Expression". multi-modal .h5 files carry Gene Expression Antibody Capture features, load gene side read ADT side separately read_tenx_h5_adt(), attach SingleCellsMultiModal object via add_adt_counts_sc().
code: features <- data.table(id = var$gene_id, name = var$ensembl_id) h5_tenx <- file.path(base, "sample_a_10x.h5") write_tenx_h5_sc(   f_path = h5_tenx,   counts = counts_a,   barcodes = obs[idx_a]$cell_id,   features = features,   version = "v3" )  sc_10x <- SingleCells(dir_data = file.path(base, "store_10x")) sc_10x <- load_tenx_h5(   object = sc_10x,   h5_path = h5_tenx,   sc_qc_param = qc,   feature_type = "Gene Expression",   .verbose = FALSE ) sc_10x #> Single cell experiment (Single Cells). #>   No cells (original): 500 #>    To keep n: 500 #>   No genes: 100 #>   HVG calculated: FALSE #>   PCA calculated: FALSE #>   Other embeddings: none #>   KNN generated: FALSE #>   SNN generated: FALSE #>   MAGIC imputed: none #>   Stale artefacts: none features_b <- data.table(   id = var$gene_id,   name = var$ensembl_id,   feature_type = "Gene Expression" ) h5_tenx_b <- file.path(base, "sample_b_10x.h5") write_tenx_h5_sc(   f_path = h5_tenx_b,   counts = counts_b,   barcodes = obs[idx_b]$cell_id,   features = features_b,   version = "v3" )  ps_10x <- prescan_tenx_h5_files(   h5_paths = c(sample_a = h5_tenx, sample_b = h5_tenx_b),   feature_type = "Gene Expression",   gene_universe = "intersection",   .verbose = FALSE )  sc_multi_10x <- SingleCells(dir_data = file.path(base, "store_multi_10x")) sc_multi_10x <- load_multi_tenx_h5(   object = sc_multi_10x,   prescan_result = ps_10x,   sc_qc_param = qc,   .verbose = FALSE ) sc_multi_10x #> Single cell experiment (Single Cells). #>   No cells (original): 1000 #>    To keep n: 1000 #>   No genes: 100 #>   HVG calculated: FALSE #>   PCA calculated: FALSE #>   Other embeddings: none #>   KNN generated: FALSE #>   SNN generated: FALSE #>   MAGIC imputed: none #>   Stale artefacts: none  # cells per sample get_sc_obs(sc_multi_10x)[, .N, by = exp_id] #>      exp_id     N #>      <char> <int> #> 1: sample_a   500 #> 2: sample_b   500

title: Reference mapping with Symphony
text: well-annotated reference data set, usually want re-whole pipeline… QC, HVG selection, PCA, batch correction, clustering, manual annotation… every time new sample lands desk. Symphony (Kang, et al., 2021) addresses compressing reference small set cached terms can used map new query cells coordinate system single shot, need retain original reference cells query time. vignette walks full workflow: Build reference two PBMC data sets (pbmc3k + pbmc4k), correcting batch effect Harmony v2 annotating cell types scType. Compress reference SymphonyReference snapshot cell type labels . Load third PBMC data set (pbmc8k) query, project reference, transfer labels via kNN majority vote. read batch correction vignette introductory vignette, please first; vignette assumes familiarity .

title: Reference mapping with Symphony
text: use pbmc3k + pbmc4k pair batch correction vignette. Two batches broad cell type composition clear technical difference exactly situation Symphony designed : reference learns batch correction , correction can applied future queries without rerunning Harmony. Standard QC: mitochondrial gene proportions, library complexity, MAD-based outlier detection. block essentially Harmony v2 path batch correction vignette: pick HVGs, run PCA, run Harmony v2, build neighbour graph corrected embedding. use Harmony v2 throughout. Version 1 still available via harmony_sc() params_sc_harmony(), v2 preferable settings (see batch correction vignette reasoning). Cluster Harmony-corrected graph, annotate clusters scType using PBMC marker set. mirrors annotation block PBMC vignette. Marker set: scType scoring per-cluster assignment: Quick sanity check reference: batches mixed, cell types separated.   Let’s see sensible cell type labels canonical markers  now everything need: HVG selection, batch annotation, cell type labels obs table. build_symphony_ref() re-runs PCA Harmony internally using supplied HVGs, caches loadings, centroids compression terms (Nr, C) needed query mapping. Pass label_columns snapshot one obs columns – scType annotation – reference downstream label transfer. note apparent duplication: yes, indeed, PCA + Harmony run inside build_symphony_ref(), even though just ran HVGs preprocessing block . deliberate. standard pipeline keeps embeddings SingleCells object streams disk; Symphony reference keeps self-contained, -memory copy everything needs project queries without reference cells. code: var_q <- get_sc_var(sc_query)  gs_q <- list(   MT = var_q[grepl("^MT-", column1), gene_id],   Ribo = var_q[grepl("^RPS|^RPL", column1), gene_id] )  sc_query <- gene_set_proportions_sc(   sc_query,   gs_q,   streaming = FALSE,   .verbose = TRUE )  qc_df_q <- sc_query[[c("cell_id", "lib_size", "nnz", "MT")]]  metrics_q <- list(   log10_lib_size = log10(qc_df_q$lib_size),   log10_nnz = log10(qc_df_q$nnz),   MT = qc_df_q$MT )  qc_q <- run_cell_qc(   metrics = metrics_q,   cells_to_keep = get_cells_to_keep(sc_query),   directions = c(     log10_lib_size = "twosided",     log10_nnz = "twosided",     MT = "above"   ),   threshold = 3 )  sc_query[["outlier"]] <- qc_q$combined sc_query <- set_cells_to_keep(   sc_query,   qc_df_q[!qc_q$combined, cell_id] )

title: Reference mapping with Symphony
text: map_symphony_query() actual projection: query cells standardised reference’s per-HVG means SDs, projected reference PCA loadings, assigned soft cluster weights reference centroids. weights drive cached MoE batch correction, putting query cells z_corr coordinate system reference. Genes matched name. Missing HVGs treated zero columns; function reports many missing. Even though pbmc8k single batch, still pass batch_column = "exp_id" Symphony applies cached correction relative reference batches. Setting batch_column = NULL skips correction entirely (resulting symphony embedding equals symphony_pca). query now carries three embeddings: "symphony" (z_corr, corrected embedding), "symphony_pca" (z_pca, pre-correction), "symphony_r" (soft cluster assignments, one column per reference centroid). neighbour graph UMAP corrected embedding give us something plot :

title: Reference mapping with Symphony
text: transfer_labels_symphony() kNN majority vote reference’s z_corr (searchable index) using query’s "symphony" embedding. reads labels directly reference’s stored labels slot – one populated via label_columns = "sc_type" build time. text: Calculates AUC-type score akin AUCell across gene sets, see Aibar et al. Three statistics offer, consuming within-cell ranking weighting differently. "wilcox" (default) AUC derived Mann-Whitney U statistic full ranking; null sits 0.5 gene set size, makes good fit pathway activity. "recovery" recovery-curve AUC rank cutoff, .e. actual AUCell statistic Aibar, et al., top-heavy: genes inside top max_rank cell contribute. "ap" average precision, top-heavy three, null tracks gene set prevalence, raw values comparable across gene sets different size unless standardise . Data can streamed chunks 50k cells per loaded one go.

eq ,j} a_{ik} a_{kj}}{\min(k_i, k_j) + 1 - a_{ij}}$$ Signed, v1: $$TOM_{ij} =  rac{a_{ij} + \sum_{k

eq ,j} a_{ik} a_{kj}}{\min(k_i, k_j) + a_{ij}} ight)$$ Signed, v2: $$TOM_{ij} = 0.5 \left( a_{ij} +  rac{\sum_{k

what: Generate a weighted nearest neighbour (WNN) graph — generate_wnn_graph_sc
title: Generate a weighted nearest neighbour (WNN) graph — generate_wnn_graph_sc
text: function implements approach Hao et al., generate weighted nearest neighbour graph given two 'omics modalities (example RNA ADT). Per-cell modality weights computed comparing within- cross-modality neighbourhood distances, weights used fuse two modalities single multimodal kNN graph. per-modality kNN graphs always recomputed internally chosen embeddings knn_range neighbours (see params_sc_wnn()); kNN graphs previously stored object via find_neighbours_sc() reused, WNN requires larger candidate pool default neighbour search. result stored object's other_data "wnn", containing fused kNN graph SingleCellNearestNeighbour (kernelised pseudo-distance metric), sNN graph igraph table per-cell modality weights. graph can subsequently used clustering 2D embedding via "wnn" modality.

title: Generate a weighted nearest neighbour (WNN) graph — generate_wnn_graph_sc
code: generate_wnn_graph_sc(   object,   modality_1 = "rna",   modality_2 = "adt",   embd_to_use_1 = "pca",   embd_to_use_2 = "pca",   no_embd_to_use_1 = NULL,   no_embd_to_use_2 = NULL,   wnn_params = params_sc_wnn(),   full_snn = TRUE,   pruning = 1/15,   snn_similarity = "jaccard",   seed = 42L,   .verbose = TRUE )

title: Generate a weighted nearest neighbour (WNN) graph — generate_wnn_graph_sc
text: object SingleCellsMultiModal class add WNN. modality_1 String. First modality. Defaults "rna". modality_2 String. Second modality. Defaults "adt". embd_to_use_1 String. embedding use first modality. Must available object modality_1. Defaults "pca". embd_to_use_2 String. embedding use second modality. Must available object modality_2. Defaults "pca". no_embd_to_use_1 Optional integer. Number embedding dimensions use embd_to_use_1. NULL, used. no_embd_to_use_2 Optional integer. Number embedding dimensions use embd_to_use_2. NULL, used. wnn_params Named list. Controls parameters WNN generation, see params_sc_wnn(). full_snn Boolean. Shall full shared nearest neighbour graph generated generates edges cells instead neighbours. pruning Numeric. Weights threshold set 0 generation sNN graph. Seurat uses example 1/15 k = 20. snn_similarity String. One c("rank", "jaccard"). Jaccard similarity calculates Jaccard neighbours, whereas rank method calculates edge weights based ranking shared neighbours. rank method, weight determined finding shared neighbour lowest combined rank across cells, lower-ranked (closer) shared neighbours result higher edge weights methods produce weights normalised range ⁠[0, 1]⁠. seed Integer. reproducibility. .verbose Boolean integer. Controls verbosity returns run times. FALSE -> quiet, TRUE 1L -> normal verbosity, 2L -> detailed verbosity.

title: Run t-SNE on a SingleCells/MetaCells object — tsne_sc
text: Wrapper around manifoldsR::tsne() SingleCells MetaCells classes. t-SNE produces low-dimensional embedding emphasises local neighbourhood structure. Distances well-separated clusters -interpreted quantitatively, common claim t-SNE discards global structure UMAP preserves largely artefact default initialisations rather property loss functions . use_knn = FALSE (default), kNN graph already stored object reused. Otherwise neighbours computed chosen embedding. Two approximation strategies available via approx_type: "bh" (Barnes-Hut) classical O(n log n) approximation works well across wide range dataset sizes; "fft" (interpolation-based, FIt-SNE) scales better large datasets. perplexity controls bandwidth Gaussian kernel used compute affinities within neighbour set (typical values 5-50). pre-computed kNN supplied via use_knn = TRUE, perplexity longer drives neighbour retrieval still shapes affinity distribution retrieved neighbours; values close kNN size produce poor results. tSNE particular rule thumb set k 3 * perplexity. `k ≤ perplexity“ algorithm behave properly anymore, thus, throw error.

UMAP produces low-dimensional embedding emphasises local neighbourhood structure computationally efficient via negative-sampling-based optimisation. de facto default visualising single-cell data, though claims preserves global structure substantially better t-SNE well supported; matched initialisation (e.g. PCA Laplacian Eigenmaps), two methods behave similarly global geometry, interpreted primarily views local structure. use_knn = TRUE (default), kNN graph already stored object (via find_neighbours_sc()) reused, avoids recomputing nearest neighbours keeps UMAP consistent downstream sNN-based clustering. kNN present, neighbours computed chosen embedding fly.
